name: Illinois
overview: Illinois offers a nonrefundable income-tax credit for owner property taxes, alongside homestead exemptions and senior tax deferral.

programs.name: Illinois Property Tax Credit
programs.incomeDefinition: Adjusted gross income and federal filing status.
programs.incomeLimits: Not allowed above $500,000 joint or $250,000 for other returns.
programs.maximumBenefit: 5% of eligible Illinois real-estate taxes, limited to income-tax liability.
programs.formulaSummary: Five percent of qualifying property taxes paid on the principal residence.
eligibilityNotes: Must own and reside in the qualifying Illinois property.
Prior assessment-year taxes are commonly paid during the income-tax year.
interactions: No refund or carryforward for unused credit.
programs.programYear: Property taxes paid during 2025; 2025 income-tax return.

programs.name: Senior Citizens Real Estate Tax Deferral
programs.ageRule: Age 65 by June 1 of the application year.
programs.incomeLimits: $75,000 for property-tax year 2025 under current agency guidance.
programs.maximumBenefit: Up to $7,500 deferred annually, subject to equity and program conditions.
programs.formulaSummary: State pays approved taxes as a loan secured by a lien; interest and repayment apply.
eligibilityNotes: Ownership/occupancy, insurance, equity and delinquency conditions apply.

researchNotes: Deferrals are loans, not credits or permanent tax savings.
County homestead exemptions and senior assessment freezes are separate contextual relief.
